title: Test two one-call BIT batching models on the pinned caller
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The first replay checks two standard IDLE groups sharing one scalar-role map. For the selected coordinate matching, the independent pulse rank is 14 and the merged pulse rank is 8. A 5,040-matching control gives merged ranks 8 through 14. The one-common-map obstruction covers the stated nonscalar pair even with allowed scalar mixing. A separate complete-domain rank argument rules out one neutral grade-eight owner wrapper on the named 131/196 clock-pair family.

## Task and overlap

Both tests bind #7830 at 87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15. #7873 concerns QUERY derivative rank. These use distinct physical and joint-role IDLE assumptions and include exact controls for a purported single-map batching route.

## Validation and credit

The two standalone replay.py commands authenticate exact public inputs, match directed bills, check both formal caller orientations and replay the 798-event reduced control and literal orbit/reader chronology. Both clean-copy runs passed with corruption controls. Read the subpackage notes for precise proof and scope. OpenAI Codex assisted. Retained contributors are credited in the packet.

## Open next questions

Non-neutral wrappers, role-dependent mixing, new tagged fields, changed exterior events and larger paid interfaces remain open.
